results.title: Recent Advances in Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Intelligent Automation and Control of Water Environment Systems
results.content: In [Section 2](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-1702/13/6/503#sec2-machines-13-00503), this paper introduces the coordination mechanisms and game-theoretic foundations for multi-agent systems, providing the theoretical underpinnings for distributed decision-making; [Section 3](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-1702/13/6/503#sec3-machines-13-00503) reviews the evolution of MADRL, focusing on training paradigms and modeling frameworks in dynamic and partially observable environments; [Section 4](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-1702/13/6/503#sec4-machines-13-00503) proposes a cross-domain collaborative control architecture tailored to water systems, addressing structural heterogeneity and operational complexity; [Section 5](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-1702/13/6/503#sec5-machines-13-00503) presents MADRL-based applications in four key water system scenarios, namely, urban drainage control, distributed water resource management, hydropower regulation, and autonomous monitoring with path planning; [Section 6](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-1702/13/6/503#sec6-machines-13-00503) investigates the generalization capabilities of MADRL in complex system settings and its integration with digital twin technologies; [Section 7](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-1702/13/6/503#sec7-machines-13-00503) outlines future research directions for MADRL-driven intelligent control in water systems; and [Section 8](https://www.mdpi.com/2075-1702/13/6/503#sec8-machines-13-00503) concludes this paper by summarizing the key findings and offering critical research insights. results.title: A survey on state-of-the-art experimental simulations for privacy-preserving federated learning in intelligent networking
results.content: # A survey on state-of-the-art experimental simulations for privacy-preserving federated learning in intelligent networking. Federated learning (FL) provides a collaborative framework that enables intelligent networking devices to train a shared model without the need to share local data. Our review is structured around key sections, including the introduction of FL concepts, the background of FL applied in networking, and experimental simulations covering networking for FL and FL for networking. **Citation:** Seyha Ros, Prohim Tam, Inseok Song, Seungwoo Kang, Seokhoon Kim. results.title: TRiSM for Agentic AI: A Review of Trust, Risk, and Security Management in LLM-based Agentic Multi-Agent Systems
results.content: # TRiSM for Agentic AI: A Review of Trust, Risk, and Security Management in LLM-based Agentic Multi-Agent Systems. Agentic AI systems, built upon large language models (LLMs) and deployed in multi-agent configurations, are redefining intelligence, autonomy, collaboration, and decision-making across enterprise and societal domains. This review presents a structured analysis of Trust, Risk, and Security Management (TRiSM) in the context of LLM-based Agentic Multi-Agent Systems (AMAS). We then adapt and extend the AI TRiSM framework for Agentic AI, structured around four key pillars: Governance, Explainability, ModelOps, and Privacy/Security , each contextualized to the challenges of multi-agent LLM systems. A novel risk taxonomy is proposed to capture the unique threats and vulnerabilities of Agentic AI, ranging from coordination failures to prompt-based adversarial manipulation. We further discuss strategies for improving explainability in Agentic AI , as well as approaches to enhancing security and privacy through encryption, adversarial robustness, and regulatory compliance.

results.title: Robustness in deep learning models for medical diagnostics
results.content: The current study investigates the robustness of deep learning models for accurate medical diagnosis systems with a specific focus on their ability to maintain performance in the presence of adversarial or noisy inputs. We examine factors that may influence model reliability, including model complexity, training data quality, and hyperparameters; we also examine security concerns related to adversarial attacks that aim to deceive models along with privacy attacks that seek to extract sensitive information. This paper concludes by discussing limitations in the existing literature and possible future research directions to continue enhancing the status of this research topic, particularly in the medical domain, with the aim of ensuring that AI systems are trustworthy, reliable, and stable. Robustness is an essential property of deep learning models that are used in medical systems, and such models must support a wide range of inputs, such as different types of medical images or patient data, while also having the ability to consistently provide accurate diagnoses under various conditions (Apostolidis and Papakostas 2021 A survey on adversarial deep learning robustness in medical image analysis.
